short: Theodosius I's death in January 395 split the empire between his sons Arcadius and Honorius, a division that never again reversed.
full:
Theodosius I, the last emperor to rule the entire Roman world, died at Milan on 17 January 395. His two sons succeeded him separately: Arcadius, already Augustus in the east since 383, took the eastern provinces from Constantinople, while the young Honorius, under the guardianship of the general Stilicho, took the west from Milan and later Ravenna.

Earlier emperors, including Diocletian's tetrarchs and Valentinian I and Valens, had shared rule between east and west before, always with the possibility of reunification. After 395 the two halves kept separate courts, separate armies and increasingly separate fates: the eastern empire endured for another millennium, while the western empire succumbed to internal collapse and Germanic settlement within a century.
